title: Chicken 65
summary: Chicken thighs are marinated in yoghurt and spices, coated in a thin starchy crust, then fried until deeply crisp and tossed through a quick sizzling tempering of curry leaves and garlic.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm pieces

ingredients.note: or 1½ tsp paprika + ½ tsp hot chilli powder

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
small red onion, sliced into rings

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, lemon juice, salt and chopped curry leaves. Cover and marinate in the fridge for anywhere from 30 minutes up to 8 hours - the yoghurt's acidity gently tenderises the meat while the spices work their way in.

steps.title: Coat in the flours
steps.text: Just before frying, sprinkle over the cornflour and rice flour and mix until it forms a thick, clinging coat, adding a tablespoon or two of water only if the mixture looks dry. The combination of the two flours gives the eventual crust its characteristic crisp, slightly brittle texture.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil to a depth of about 4 cm into the heavy pot or wok and heat to 175°C, checking with a frying thermometer. Getting the temperature right before frying matters - too cool and the coating turns greasy rather than crisp.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Fry the chicken in 3 batches, separating the pieces as they go in so they don't clump together, for 4-5 minutes per batch until deep red-brown, crisp and reaching 74°C inside the largest piece. Drain each batch on the wire rack and let the oil return to temperature between batches.

steps.title: Make the tempering
steps.text: In a small frying pan, heat the tablespoon of oil over medium-high heat, then add the curry leaves - stand back, as they spit in hot oil - followed by the green chillies and garlic. Cook for 30-60 seconds until the leaves turn crisp and the garlic is pale gold, then toss straight through the fried chicken.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the chicken onto a plate with the tempering scattered over, and serve with the sliced red onion rings and lemon wedges alongside. The sharp onion and fresh lemon cut nicely through the chicken's heat and crunch.

tips: Add the cornflour and rice flour only just before frying - mixed in too early, the coating can turn gluey rather than crisp.
Keep the oil at a steady 165°C by checking with a thermometer; letting it drift too low is the most common reason Chicken 65 ends up soggy instead of crunchy.
Don't overcrowd the pot - frying in batches keeps the oil temperature steady and each piece properly crisp.
Stand well back when the curry leaves hit the hot oil, as they spit.
safety: Check a piece reaches 74°C in the centre before serving, especially the largest ones in each batch.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh and crisp, but leftovers will keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot oven or air fryer until piping hot and 74°C throughout, rather than microwaving, to bring back some crispness. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
